newsitem.title: USA: Dow falls in cautious session, techs extend slump.
newsitem.headline: Dow falls in cautious session, techs extend slump.

text.p: Wall Street stocks ended broadly lower on Wednesday, as investors adopted a cautious stance amid heightened concerns about corporate earnings and ahead of a critical economic report.

The Dow industrials dipped 43 points to close unofficially at 7270. Technology stocks led the decline, extending their slump, but in contrast to recent sessions, the market's weakness broadened well beyond the beleaguered tech sector.
Adding to a recent spate of earnings warnings today was PepsiCo Inc.
Analysts said Pepsi presented weaker-than-expected earnings growth projections during a meeting with Wall Street analysts today.
Shares in Pepsi fell 2-3/8 to 35-7/8 in New York Stock Exchange activity. The stock was the second most active on the NYSE, with more than 8.6 million shares changing hands.

With several recent earnings warnings still ringing in Wall Street's ears, analysts said it was understandable that investors had opted to draw back from the market, particularly with the May wage and payrolls report looming on Friday.

"No one is going to want to be a hero in front of the employment number," said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management. "This market has discounted an awful lot of good news and has no margin for error in earnings or the economy or interest rates."
Selling pressure weighed heaviest on the tech sector, the source of the highest profile earnings warnings.

Intel Corp, which last Friday warned Wall Street about weaker near-term prospects, fell 2-1/2 to 142-1/2. That forecast has weighed on the entire computer hardware group due to the nearly universal presence of Intel's products.

The worries were sufficient to send rumors swirling that personal computer makers were also about to begin issuing warnings. One company, Gateway 2000 Inc late in the day refuted rumors that it planned such a warning.
Shares in Gateway fell 1/2 to 61-1/2 but slipped as low as 57 during the session. Compaq Computer Corp fell 1-1/2 to 98-1/2 and Dow component International Business Machines Corp fell one to 83-3/8.
"The love-hate relationship with techs continues," said U.S. Clearing Corp vice president Dick Stein. "Right now, we're in the hate phase."

Analysts generally expect the market to maintain its tentative tone at least through the next session. Friday's payrolls report, several noted, will be the last such report released ahead of the Federal Reserve's July policy meeting.
"The prudent thing to do in the equities market is to raise some cash ahead of a number like this," Orlando said. "That's what we have done."
Among individual issues, Iomega Corp rose one to 20-1/4 and was the NYSE's most active issue on volume of more than 10 million shares.
Late in the day the company declined to comment on the move as a matter of policy. Iomega issued the statement after the NYSE requested an explanation for the unusual activity.

H.F. Ahmanson and Co rose 1-1/4 to 41-1/2 after the company dropped its hostile takeover bid for Great Western Financial Corp. The move clears the way for Great Western's planned merger with Washington Mutual Inc.
Shares in Great Western gained 1-3/8 to 48-3/4. Western Mutual rose 1-1/16 to 54-13/16.
The S&P 500 index fell 5.37 points to 840.11.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.24 points to 1379.67.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
